user.title: Connect to the CTC controller
user.description: Modbus TCP must be enabled on the controller (Settings → Communication → BMS).

model.title: Controller model
model.description: The controller answers every register whether or not the hardware behind it exists, so which subsystems you have cannot be detected reliably. The model sets sensible defaults; tick anything optional you actually have fitted. You can change this later in the integration's options.

setpoints.title: Writable entities (optional)
setpoints.description:
The integration is read-only unless you tick this.

⚠️ Writable entities change the controller's **stored parameters**, and CTC's BMS manual warns: *"These parameters must not be changed a lot of times. If you do so you risk breaking the controller of the heat pump installation. There is a limit to the amount of write cycles!"*

That is fine for settings you change by hand now and then — room temperature, hot water mode, blocking a heat pump. It is **not** safe to drive them from an automation on a timer or an electricity price signal: at one write every 15 minutes you would reach the controller's likely write-cycle limit within a few years.

You can change this later in the integration's options.

data_description.setpoints: A curated set: room temperature setpoints, night reduction, hot water stop temperature and mode, compressor max RPS, heating modes and programs, and blocking a heat pump.

error.cannot_connect: The controller did not answer. Check the address, that Modbus TCP is enabled, and that nothing else is talking to it.

data.heat_pumps: Heat pumps to create devices for
data.zones: Heating systems (zones) to create devices for

data_description.heat_pumps: Detection can miss hardware that is idle (e.g. compressors in summer read 0 everywhere); force-enable it here.
data_description.model: Only labels the controller device. Which subsystems exist is controlled below — changing the model here does not re-tick them.
data_description.subsystems: A controller answers the solar, pool and wood-boiler registers whether or not that hardware is installed, so this cannot be detected. Untick anything you do not have: its device and entities disappear and its registers stop being polled.
data_description.setpoints: ⚠️ These write to the controller's stored parameters, which have a limited number of write cycles — CTC warns that changing them too often risks breaking the controller. Safe to change by hand; do not drive them from an automation on a timer or a price signal. Untick for a strictly read-only integration.
